title: Turkey vs. Italy in the 2026/27 Nations League: All You Need to Know
seoTitle: Turkey vs. Italy Nations League 2026/27: What to Know
subtitle: Second-round match in Group A1 takes place in Bursa and could impact Euro 2028 qualification
excerpt: Turkey and Italy face off this Monday at 3:45 PM (Brasília time) at the Bursa Metropolitan Stadium, in a second-round Nations League match.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Turkey and Italy face off this Monday at 3:45 PM (Brasília time) at the Bursa Metropolitan Stadium, in a match valid for the second round of the 2026/27 Nations League. The clash gains prominence as both teams seek to bounce back after defeats in their opening matches.

Reason for high demand

Following Turkey's 1-0 defeat to France and Italy's 2-0 loss to Belgium, fans are searching for information about the upcoming duel, which could influence qualification for Euro 2028.

Predicted Lineups

For Turkey, starting goalkeeper Çakir is suspended; the team is expected to start with Bayindir between the posts. The midfield features Real Madrid's Arda Güler as the main reference. The announced formation includes Bayindir, Çelik, Demiral, and Bardakci; Aydin, Ozcan, Yuksek, Arda Güler, and Kadioglu; Uzun and Ylmaz, under the command of Vincenzo Montella.

For Italy, Roberto Mancini is expected to make at least five changes. Predicted changes include the inclusions of Kayode and Bastoni in defense, with Barella and Tonali possibly rested. The list includes Donnarumma; Kayode, Mancin, Bastoni, and Calafiori; Frattesi, Barella (or Tonali), and Mandragora; Raspadori, Maldini, and Scamacca.

What's at Stake

The match is part of the group stage, which runs until November 17, 2026. The best performers advance to the quarter-finals between March 25 and 30, 2027, and the final phase is scheduled for the week of June 9, 2027. The results also influence qualification for Euro 2028, to be played in England and the Republic of Ireland, and the European Qualifiers playoffs for the 2030 World Cup.

Where to Watch

The game will be broadcast live on sportv and Disney+ channels, with real-time coverage of the main plays on the ge website. The referee for the match will be Michael Oliver from England.

Coaches' Expectations

Vincenzo Montella highlighted the need to improve ball possession compared to the last match against France. Roberto Mancini, in turn, emphasized the importance of staying calm and reacting well against a team considered strong, like Belgium, in the opening fixture.

With information from ge.
